summary: Bind browser actions to their original context, verify deployment and variable transport, and use explicit directory presentation contracts with permission-based administration.
userImpact: Adding and uploading native JSON variables uses the same serialized engine contract as editing existing variables.
Process navigation discards action drafts belonging to the previous instance, including when both instances use the same engine.
Bulk variable writes and completed-history snapshots retain prototype-like variable names as ordinary own fields.
Reserved variable names are rejected before a bulk write can silently omit them.
Late authentication responses cannot restore an older browser session or replace newer permissions.
Save-and-deploy cannot continue against a replacement project, file selection or session.
Unsafe or out-of-range numeric variable writes are rejected instead of rounding or becoming null.
Versioned engine deployments reject content or snapshot drift before contacting the engine.
User administration reads an explicit account access preset without using compatibility role fields for authorization.
Changing users, sessions or permissions discards old directory loads and lifecycle confirmations.
Inherited access is shown inactive after membership expiry or group archival; incomplete ownership metadata does not enable manual user creation.
Locked directory accounts expose the permission-gated unlock action without requiring legacy counters.
Profile edits no longer resend unchanged account access or active status and overwrite intervening lifecycle changes.
Account status changes use audited lifecycle actions; legacy profile/delete paths cannot bypass status, ownership, reason or recovery checks, and LDAP reactivation remains directory-owned.
Shared SaaS profile names stay at their identity/provisioning provider boundary; normalized timestamps and controlled edit fields keep directory presentation consistent.
Process drafts and deployment continuations discard older session and permission state even when the URL, account or engine ID stays the same.
An older 401 refresh cannot replay a request under a replacement login or clear its local state; private caches are discarded on same-account session replacement and permission changes.
Session startup makes one refresh attempt for an expired session and stops on other failures; a pending login-page bootstrap cannot continue after switching tenants.
Runtime configuration rejects redirects so a same-origin configuration URL cannot delegate API or module settings to another origin.
Saved diagram views load the canonical project-bound revision endpoint and select the requested file by stable identity; missing revisions no longer display a sibling file or the editable draft.
Local file versions and Git commit snapshots use separate caches, preventing an equal ID from supplying the wrong preview or restore readiness.
Restoring a file version changes only the selected file; sibling drafts and file-version history remain independent.
Pending restore stops when its file, version, session or permissions change, and an unverified preceding save cannot permit restore.
Saving or restoring one file preserves sibling saved baselines and unsaved drafts. Create Version refuses obsolete preparation and unverified responses.
Publish uses the saved draft tree without including unsaved siblings. Dirty status recognizes renames, moves, deletion markers and conflicting snapshots.

instructions: Upgrade the qualified shared/frontend/backend host composition together; no database schema or historical data repair is required.

Clients that change account status through profile PUT must use the deactivate/reactivate endpoints with an administrator reason. Compatibility DELETE requests also require a reason body; unchanged isActive profile echoes remain accepted and are never persisted.

changes: The frontend write adapter accepts parsed native JSON values and serializes them once for the engine. The external HTTP API and scalar/Java Object contracts are unchanged.

Proxy deployment requests with options.vcsCommitId return HTTP 409 when project ownership or the exact selected file snapshots do not match. Unversioned requests no longer infer an unverified commit link.

Directory summaries and effective-access responses add the informational bootstrapAccess enum. Existing compatibility fields remain available; frontend actions continue to use permission snapshots and server guards.
Security enforcement: status-changing profile PUT returns 409; compatibility DELETE requires the lifecycle reason body and uses audited deactivation; direct SCIM/LDAP profile overrides are rejected.

The existing commit-files endpoint returns a shared strict snapshot DTO and binds commit reads to the authorized project. Both saved-diagram views use that endpoint; stable file identity takes priority over names.

File restore uses POST /vcs-api/projects/{projectId}/commits/{commitId}/files/{fileId}/restore with the existing restore permission. Older hosts reject that route without whole-project effects; the client has no legacy fallback. Checkpoints keep the existing file-save marker and explicit file-version scope. The original project restore endpoint remains supported. Ambiguous stored snapshots reach validation without timestamp-based selection.
Publish and dirty-status endpoints preserve HTTP 409 for unavailable or conflicting saved baselines; publish requires a saved draft owned by the requested project and user.

notes: No database schema or stored-variable changes.

security: Engine selection, variable-value authorization, tenant routing and stale-response guards remain enforced.
Process-local action state is remounted on instance navigation instead of being retargeted to another process.
Unmounted action callbacks cannot refetch or notify through a later tenant/process route; already issued operations retain their original target.
Browser action lifetimes use monotonically increasing revisions; server authentication, authorization and tenant boundaries remain enforced.
Commit/project/snapshot validation completes before any versioned engine deployment effect.
Lifecycle audits use the existing exact-row append capability inside the transaction; unbound or wrong-row audit inserts remain denied under forced RLS, with no database-policy or grant changes.

Engine callbacks are checked before dispatch and on settlement using their render, mount and browser-session lifetime. Shared refreshes are session/tenant-bound; cancelled callers never replay and server authorization remains authoritative.
The same-origin runtime configuration boundary rejects redirects before contacting their destination; direct same-origin documents retain explicit API-origin selection.

Commit snapshot reads bind the authorized project in SQL; restore updates require the target row to belong to that project. Historical diagram content stays separate from draft autosave, with no authorization, database policy or grant relaxation.
Mixed-resolver authorization actions require explicit scope selection; single-project VCS status resolves the requested project. No grant or database policy change.

Publication rejects foreign project/owner/tree references and conflicting identities before changing main. Dirty-status baseline lookup is project-bound. Existing grants, database policies and migration floors are unchanged.

customerDocumentation.reason: Repairs the existing variable controls without adding a new configuration or administrator procedure.

knownLimitations: Local request-shape and engine fixture checks do not establish live SaaS tenant isolation or staging installation.

In pooled SaaS, administrator profile-name editing is unavailable because a tenant-filtered query cannot establish global provisioning ownership. Update names at the authenticated identity or provisioning provider.
rollback: Restore the previous qualified frontend and backend hosts; the previous variable, session and deployment wiring defects may recur.
validation: Focused frontend adapter, route, editor, retry, modification and history regressions.
Real pinned Operaton round trip using the actual frontend writer and shared runtime/task/history reader.
Frontend host typecheck and packed entrypoint verification; release workflow, classifier, aggregate, package-version and documentation contracts.
Full protected exact-candidate, browser and live two-tenant acceptance remain separate requirements.
Authentication, two-stage deployment, numeric parser and variable adapter regression tests.
Actual PostgreSQL deployment revision lookup and drift/foreign-project rejection.
Admin list/detail navigation, revocation, metadata uncertainty and strict API response-binding tests.
User directory service and current membership presentation on SQL.js and owned PostgreSQL fixtures.
Forced PostgreSQL RLS tests exercise audited deactivation/reactivation/session revocation, guarded compatibility paths and strict profile DTO serialization.
Deferred session/permission/engine transitions, positive same-authority refresh, StrictMode, shared refresh cancellation and owned native loopback HTTP transport sequences.
Session bootstrap through the actual auth provider, service, API client and HTTP interceptor: one refresh owner, no refresh on non-401 failures, and tenant-switch refusal before the next request.
Owned native HTTP configuration origins prove redirect refusal, required startup failure, optional fallback and explicit cross-origin API selection without following a redirect.
Canonical snapshot adapter and viewer regressions, project-authorized route/restore tests and actual PostgreSQL sibling-project snapshot denial.
Production-built BPMN/DMN viewer and missing-snapshot browser assertions against owned local HTTP responses; the viewer selects the bundled modern WOFF icon face.
Actual PostgreSQL route, restore, VCS checkpoint and history/backfill integration with sibling-file/project denials; deferred autosave/restore browser component lifetime cases.
Actual PostgreSQL scoped-save/restore dirty-state and identity regressions, explicit authorization resolver contracts and deferred Create Version lifetime/acknowledgement checks.

Actual PostgreSQL scoped save to publish to deployment-revision verification, repeated publish/new draft inheritance, metadata/tombstone/duplicate/content-drift negatives and cyclic folder ancestry. Git import/push complete-save callers remain covered locally.
